## 1. Ziconotide (Prialt)

- **INN/generic:** Ziconotide (as ziconotide acetate) | **Brand:** Prialt
- **Cyclization type:** Disulfide-rich **ω-conotoxin (ICK / inhibitor cystine knot)**. 25-aa peptide with 6 cysteines forming **3 disulfide bridges** (connectivity Cys1–Cys4, Cys2–Cys5, Cys3–Cys6) arranged in a **cystine-knot topology** (two disulfides + the connecting backbone form a ring through which the third disulfide threads). It is NOT head-to-tail (backbone) cyclic — the constraint is entirely from the three-disulfide knot.
- **Origin:** **Venom-derived** — synthetic (chemically synthesized) equivalent of the naturally occurring peptide from marine cone snail *Conus magus*.
- **DISCOVERY METHOD:** Direct **venom/toxin isolation** — ω-conotoxin MVIIA was isolated and characterized from *Conus magus* fish-hunting cone snail venom; the drug (developer code **SNX-111**) is a synthetic reproduction of that natural peptide. Developed at Neurex Corp. (George Miljanich) → acquired by Elan. No library screening — this is classic natural-product venom pharmacology.
- **Molecular target:** **N-type voltage-gated calcium channel (Cav2.2)** — selective blocker on primary afferent nociceptive nerve terminals in the spinal cord dorsal horn, blocking excitatory neurotransmitter release.
- **Indication:** Management of **severe chronic pain** in patients requiring intrathecal therapy who are intolerant/refractory to other analgesics (incl. intrathecal morphine).
- **First approval:** **FDA — December 28, 2004**; EMA approved 2005.
- **Originator/company:** Neurex Corporation → Elan Pharmaceuticals; now marketed by **Jazz Pharmaceuticals** (US) / TerSera.
- **Route:** **Intrathecal** infusion only.
- **Notes:** 25 amino acids, polycationic; ICK/cystine-knot scaffold prototype; narrow therapeutic window with substantial CNS adverse effects.

### SyntheMol — Swanson et al., *Nature Machine Intelligence* 2024 ([DOI 10.1038/s42256-024-00809-7](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42256-024-00809-7); code [github.com/swansonk14/SyntheMol](https://github.com/swansonk14/SyntheMol))
- **Key idea:** MCTS over a combinatorial synthesis space (132,479 Enamine REAL building blocks × 13 reaction templates, ~30B compounds), guided by a property predictor. Every output ships with a 1–2 step route.

# Polymyxin-Class Antibacterials: Regulatory Approval Status & Cyclicity

## Shared architecture (all polymyxins)
Every clinically-used polymyxin is a **decapeptide lipopeptide** with three parts: a **cyclic heptapeptide ring** (residues 4–10) + an **exocyclic linear tripeptide side chain** (residues 1–3) + an **N-terminal fatty-acyl tail**. The macrocycle closes via a **lactam (amide) bond between the side-chain γ-amino group of the Dab at position 4 and the α-carboxyl of the C-terminal Thr10** — a side-chain-to-C-terminus lactam. The ring is rich in cationic 2,4-diaminobutyric acid (Dab). Mechanism is uniform: cationic Dab residues bind the anionic phosphates of lipid A/LPS in the Gram-negative outer membrane, displace Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺, and permeabilize the outer then inner membrane → cell death. # Polymyxin-Class Antibacterials: Regulatory Approval Status & Cyclicity

## Shared architecture (all polymyxins)
Every clinically-used polymyxin is a **decapeptide lipopeptide** with three parts: a **cyclic heptapeptide ring** (residues 4–10) + an **exocyclic linear tripeptide side chain** (residues 1–3) + an **N-terminal fatty-acyl tail**. The macrocycle closes via a **lactam (amide) bond between the side-chain γ-amino group of the Dab at position 4 and the α-carboxyl of the C-terminal Thr10** — a side-chain-to-C-terminus lactam. The ring is rich in cationic 2,4-diaminobutyric acid (Dab). Mechanism is uniform: cationic Dab residues bind the anionic phosphates of lipid A/LPS in the Gram-negative outer membrane, displace Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺, and permeabilize the outer then inner membrane → cell death. [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK557540/] [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7463838/] [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2907661/]

# Conformation-Aware Cyclic-Peptide Permeability: What Transfers from Small-Molecule ADMET (2024–2026)

Your R²=0.23 is essentially the *floor* of the field. Under the same data, well-tuned 2D graph models already reach R²≈0.5–0.55 (scaffold-honest) and R²≈0.66–0.77 (random split / heavy augmentation). Conformation-awareness is the *second, differentiating* win, and the literature says the payoff is mainly in out-of-distribution generalization, not in-domain R².

# Glycopeptide / Lipoglycopeptide Antibacterials — Approval Status & Cyclicity

**Key concept confirmed:** All true glycopeptide antibiotics (vancomycin family, teicoplanin, etc.) are **cyclic** — their aglycone is a nonribosomally-biosynthesized heptapeptide whose aromatic side chains are extensively **cross-linked** into a rigid, cage-like macrocyclic structure (the A-B, C-O-D, D-O-E rings). This cross-linked cyclic aglycone forms the D-Ala-D-Ala binding pocket. Lipoglycodepsipeptides like ramoplanin are cyclic via a **macrolactone (depsipeptide) ring**. ([ScienceDirect – glycopeptide overview](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/neuroscience/glycopeptide-antibiotic), [PMC6901329](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6901329/))
